findings.rationale: The POST /agents handler previously returned HTTP 201 (Created) and now returns 200 (OK). Any deployed caller (web client, CI runner, external consumer) that checks for 201 to detect a successful creation will break: it may treat the 200 as an unexpected response, fail to parse the body, or silently misclassify the result. The PR description acknowledges this is a breaking change. The compatible alternative is to keep 201, or if the team decides to standardise on 200, update all callers in the same deployment and document the change in a changelog. Since the client code is not updated in this diff, the client will break.

The PR description confirms this is intentional ("the create handler answers 200 like the rest of the module"), but it breaks existing callers without a transition period.

findings.title: Client error path for CSV export throws plain Error instead of ApiError
findings.rationale: Rule 3 requires that any `fetch` call in client code, even for non-JSON responses, throws `ApiError` on non-2xx responses so that the UI can display the server's error code and message. The new `downloadFindingsCsv` function throws a plain `Error` with a generic message, which will cause the findings panel to show a generic error and lose the status and error code from the server's `{ error: { code, message, details } }` body.

matched_title: CSV download error path throws plain Error instead of ApiError

findings.title: CSV download error path throws plain Error instead of ApiError
findings.rationale: The new `downloadFindingsCsv` function uses `fetch` directly and, on a non-2xx response, throws `new Error(...)`. The house rule (rule 3) requires that all direct `fetch` calls in `client/src/` throw `ApiError` on error, even for non-JSON responses, so that the UI can display the server's structured error (code, message, details). A plain `Error` loses the status and code, causing a generic error message in the UI.

matched_title: Error path in downloadFindingsCsv throws plain Error instead of ApiError

findings.title: Error path in downloadFindingsCsv throws plain Error instead of ApiError
findings.rationale: Rule 3 requires that client requests surface errors as `ApiError` to preserve status, code, and message from the server's structured error body. The new `downloadFindingsCsv` function uses `fetch` directly and on a non-2xx response throws `new Error(...)` with only status and statusText. This loses the server's error code and message, and the caller cannot distinguish error types. The rule explicitly states that even for non-JSON responses (like CSV downloads), the error path must throw `ApiError` with the status and the code/message read from the error body.
